FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.97  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.get_allocation()` claims to use live-updated fingerprints for allocation, but `LoadBalancer` never reads fingerprints at all. Allocation depends only on token demand, role admissibility, capacity, cost, latency, and current loads. Therefore the adaptive-routing feedback loop is functionally disconnected from load balancing. This is an architectural correctness issue because the module’s stated adaptive behavior does not occur.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either (a) incorporate fingerprint-derived utility into the load-balancing objective/constraints, e.g. task-model suitability weights based on flaw class and capability, or (b) remove the claim that allocation uses live fingerprints. If intended, add explicit scoring in `_solve_greedy()` / `_objective()` that prefers models whose fingerprints suit the task.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.95  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.80  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` for format violations instead of `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This makes event consumers unable to distinguish parse failures from format failures, despite the interface defining separate event types.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In the FORMAT branch, emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION` instead of `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED`. Add a unit test asserting the emitted event type for parseable-but-format-noncompliant responses.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.94  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.74  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.check_dispatch_feasibility()` emits `DISPATCH_BLOCKED` events but does not call `record_dispatch_block()`. Likewise, successful later dispatches are not recorded automatically. As a result, the Phase E dispatch false-positive health monitor has no data unless external callers manually maintain internal tracking, which contradicts the manager’s orchestration role.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Call `self.record_dispatch_block(model.model_id, self.fsm.current_round)` whenever dispatch is blocked, and provide/trigger a corresponding success recording path when a previously blocked model succeeds. If success detection is external, document that requirement explicitly and expose a stable hook.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.92  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.77  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` computes `mu` using `self.diminishing_returns.marginal_value(round_idx)`, while the stop predicate uses `smoothed_marginal_value()` and may use per-model aggregation. The health monitor is then fed the unsmoothed system-level `mu`, not the actual decision metric. This can produce false immune diagnoses and inconsistent telemetry: reported `mu` is not the metric that drove stopping.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Feed the health monitor and `RoundResult.marginal_value` with the same metric used operationally, preferably `smoothed_marginal_value()` or `aggregate_per_model_mu()` plus a separate raw field if needed.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa_adopt()` returns `1 - adoption_delta` with no bounds check. If `adoption_delta` is outside `[0,1]`, `kappa_adopt` can be negative or exceed 1, violating its own docstring and contaminating `kappa()`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `adoption_delta` in `add_round_findings()` or clamp `kappa_adopt` to `[0,1]`. Add tests for out-of-range values.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.89  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__()` validates only a small subset of numeric parameters. Many thresholds documented as probabilities or bounded ratios (`tau_sim`, `eta_veto`, `theta_under`, `eta_underperform`, `epsilon_rho`, `tau_mu`, `tau_novelty_stop`, `tau_novelty`, `tau_vocab_growth`, `fingerprint_ema_alpha`, etc.) can be set to nonsensical values without error, leading to silent invalid behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add full invariant validation for all bounded parameters, integer minima for window sizes/depths, and positivity checks for costs/latencies/token limits where required.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.87  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` always re-adds the locked PM to `new_map` even if the PM is not in `active_models`. This yields a role map that can include inactive models. That can desynchronize role assignment from active dispatch state and mislead consumers reading `role_map`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either enforce that PM must always be included in `active_models` unless aborting, or only include PM in `new_map` if active and fail fast otherwise.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.should_abort()` documentation says “If only PM survives, framework degrades to single-model mode,” but the implementation aborts whenever `len(_active_models) < k_min`. This only permits PM-only mode if `k_min == 1`; otherwise the documented degradation behavior does not happen. The docstring overstates behavior and can mislead integration logic.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement explicit PM-only degradation independent of `k_min`, or change the docstring to state the abort condition is controlled entirely by `k_min`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.85  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.81  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundResult.allocation` is always set to `None`, despite the result type claiming to capture “all outputs needed for cross-area communication.” This omits a key artifact from the round result and prevents downstream auditing/replay of allocation decisions.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass the actual `Allocation` into `process_round()` or store the last allocation in the manager and include it in `RoundResult`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.72  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._redundancy_target()` uses `K = len(self.models)` rather than the count of admissible or active task-executable models. When PM is excluded for `K > 1`, a critical task gets target `K`, which may be unachievable because only `K-1` models are admissible. This systematically requests impossible redundancy and guarantees unmet targets for some configurations.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Base redundancy target on admissible-capable models for that task, or at minimum on non-PM active workers when PM is excluded.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F011  
SEVERITY: 0.83  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.69  
DESCRIPTION: `_check_feasibility()` does not check redundancy-target satisfaction at all, only token feasibility, coverage, and admissibility. Yet redundancy is described as part of the allocation contract. The solver can silently fail to meet critical redundancy requirements while still reporting only a warning-free “feasible” result.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add an explicit feasibility check `sum_m a_{jm} >= r(t_j)` for each task and report violations separately.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F012  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.solve()` returns an allocation even when hard feasibility constraints are violated, merely issuing a warning. The surrounding documentation labels these as HARD constraints. Returning infeasible allocations as normal results weakens contract safety and can propagate invalid dispatch plans.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either raise an exception on hard infeasibility, or return a result object with explicit feasibility status and require the caller to acknowledge/handle it before dispatch.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F013  
SEVERITY: 0.80  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` uses single-linkage union by pairwise threshold, while the class/docstring treats equivalence as if it were a direct relation. Threshold similarity is not generally transitive, so this clustering can merge semantically dissimilar findings through a bridge item. That distorts novelty, severity aggregation, and convergence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document that clustering is single-linkage approximate grouping, or switch to a stricter clustering rule such as complete-linkage or centroid-based clustering with explicit tradeoffs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F014  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61  
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint.as_normalised_array()` can produce negative first-coordinate values when `D_decay > pool_max[0]` or if negative inputs exist, and values >1 on other coordinates if raw values exceed assumed bounds. Since config validation does not constrain fingerprint ranges, capability scores can leave `[0,1]`, contradicting docstrings.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate fingerprint fields on construction and/or clamp normalized outputs into `[0,1]`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F015  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` uses `same_type_count >= n_fail` before recording the current failure. With default `n_fail=2`, escalation occurs on the third occurrence, not the second. The validator comments acknowledge this, making the configuration name misleading relative to common interpretation of a “repetition threshold.”  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify semantics (`prior_failures_before_escalation`) or change the condition to `same_type_count + 1 >= n_fail` if the intended threshold is total occurrences including current.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F016  
SEVERITY: 0.77  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.38  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_no_findings()` docstring says “not converged unless null_expected,” but the function only checks `kappa_set(2) == 1.0` and does not test `converged()`. The validator therefore does not validate its stated property.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either rename the validator to reflect what it actually checks or assert the intended convergence behavior explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F017  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.62  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` only records failures for models present in `responses`. Missing responses for allocated/active models are ignored entirely, even though absent responses are operationally closer to failure than success. This can undercount failures and distort active model management.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Compare expected responders against active allocated models and synthesize an EMPTY/TIMEOUT-style failure when a response is missing. This requires passing allocation or expected model set into `process_round()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F018  
SEVERITY: 0.75  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.70  
DESCRIPTION: The real-time manager monitoring interface defines recovery events (`RETRY`, `REALLOCATE`, `EXCLUDE`, `ABORT`) and progress event `MODEL_RESPONSE`, but the implementation never emits them. Only some failure/progress checks are emitted. The interface contract is incomplete in implementation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit recovery action events in `get_recovery()`, emit `MODEL_RESPONSE` when responses are processed, and emit any reallocation/abort actions explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F019  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.get_ordering()` returns the original `capability_scores` computed at initial assignment and never updates them after reassignment or live fingerprint evolution. Consumers may believe they are getting current role ordering, but they get stale initialization-time scores.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute scores on demand using current active models and current fingerprints, or rename the method/data to indicate they are initial scores only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F020  
SEVERITY: 0.73  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer._objective()` treats zero-capacity models as having zero load fraction via `np.where(limits > 0, loads / limits, 0.0)`. This understates bottleneck/variance for impossible allocations involving `L <= 0`, while `model_load_fraction()` elsewhere returns `inf` for positive load on zero capacity. The inconsistency can mis-rank bad allocations.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use `inf` when `limit <= 0` and load > 0, consistently across all methods.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F021  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.34  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor` comments describe adaptive sensitivity with decay-based formula, but `effective_window()` ignores `_sensitivity_decay` entirely and only widens windows based on resolved counts. The documented adaptive model and implementation diverge materially.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement the documented decay/growth behavior or simplify the comments to match actual logic.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F022  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.apply_diagnosis()` checks for `"false_positive"` in `diagnosis.pathology.lower()`, but the generated dispatch diagnosis text is `"Dispatch false positive: ..."`, with a space, not an underscore. Therefore the pre-decompose adaptation path never fires.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Match on `"false positive"` or use structured pathology codes instead of brittle substring matching.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F023  
SEVERITY: 0.70  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.31  
DESCRIPTION: The same method includes a branch for `diagnosis.detector == "vocab_saturation"`, but no such diagnosis is generated anywhere in the artifact. This is dead adaptation logic and suggests an incomplete immune-response pipeline.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement the corresponding diagnosis generation or remove the dead branch until the pathology is actually surfaced.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F024  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.65  
DESCRIPTION: `LoadBalancer.validate_homogeneous()` claims equal distribution is optimal, but the test setup excludes the PM from work when `k>1`, so perfectly equal distribution across all `k` models is impossible by construction. The validator may still pass balance due to variance tolerance, but it does not validate the stated property.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either restate the property as “balanced across admissible worker models” or include `K=1`/all-worker setup that actually matches the claim.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F025  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.29  
DESCRIPTION: `RoundProgressionFSM.select_event()` docstring says it selects the highest-priority applicable event, but the implementation returns `MAX` only when `round_complete` is true. If max-round state is reached and the caller passes `round_complete=False`, no event is returned. The behavior is sensible, but the docstring omits that completion gating.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify that `MAX` is only applicable once the round has completed.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F026  
SEVERITY: 0.67  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.52  
DESCRIPTION: `CorrelatedFailureModel.set_vulnerability()` allows `model_i == model_j`, creating a singleton frozenset key and storing self-vulnerability even though `get_vulnerability()` hardcodes self-vulnerability to 1.0 and ignores stored values. This is inconsistent and wastes state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject self-pairs in `set_vulnerability()` or explicitly no-op them.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F027  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `pairwise_joint_failure()` and the class docstring use different formulas for correlated joint failure. The top-level class description says `p_i p_j + v_ij * min(P(i), P(j))`; the method uses `p_i p_j + v_ij * min(p_i, p_j) * (1 - max(p_i, p_j))`. This inconsistency matters because users cannot tell which model is authoritative.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update the class docstring to match the implemented bounded formula, or change the implementation to the documented formula if that was intended.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F028  
SEVERITY: 0.65  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.33  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.validate_homogeneous()` docstring says tie-breaking assigns PM, but the validator only checks one PM exists and all PM scores are equal. It does not verify which model wins or that tie-breaking is deterministic.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Assert the expected PM identity under identical fingerprints, e.g. by explicit secondary deterministic ordering or by documenting that arbitrary-but-stable selection is acceptable.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F029  
SEVERITY: 0.64  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.assign()` and `reassign()` rely on Python’s stable sort / insertion-order behavior for deterministic outcomes when both score and `_tie_break_key` are equal. There is no final stable key such as `model_id`. For identical models supplied in different input orders, results can differ.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `model_id` as a final tie-break component to guarantee order-independent determinism.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F030  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47  
DESCRIPTION: `_tokenize_for_similarity()` uses naive whitespace splitting and does not strip punctuation. Equivalent descriptions differing only by punctuation (`"overflow,"` vs `"overflow"`) become different tokens, reducing similarity and affecting convergence/novelty.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Normalize punctuation with regex tokenization or strip common punctuation before stopword filtering.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F031  
SEVERITY: 0.62  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.57  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` returns `UNDERPERFORM` without emitting a corresponding `ManagerEventType.UNDERPERFORM`, even though the event type exists. This again leaves the monitoring interface incomplete and hides an important failure mode from real-time observers.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit an `UNDERPERFORM` event when the persistence criterion triggers.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F032  
SEVERITY: 0.61  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.36  
DESCRIPTION: The file header says “All six areas ... are implemented,” but the module also contains Area 7 detector health monitoring and multiple Phase A/B/E adaptive layers. The artifact scope statement is outdated and understates what is in the file.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update the module docstring to reflect all implemented subsystems and distinguish core six areas from added extensions.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F033  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` does a linear search `next((m for m in self._models ...))` for every active model, giving avoidable O(K^2) behavior. Small K may hide it, but the code already keeps model IDs elsewhere and could do O(1) lookup.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Build and store a `model_id -> ModelSpec` dict in `RoleAssignment`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F034  
SEVERITY: 0.59  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector._compute_equivalence_classes()` is O(n^2) in finding count and recomputed across cumulative findings for every queried round. This may become expensive as rounds/findings grow. The artifact acknowledges practical bounded use, but the implementation has no memoized incremental merge strategy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Maintain incremental clustering state or index findings by flaw class/token signatures before pairwise comparison.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F035  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.27  
DESCRIPTION: Several imports are unused (`Protocol`, `Literal`, `Union`, `Tuple` partly used yes, `Any` used, `Sequence` used, `logging` used, `numpy.typing` used, but `Protocol`, `Literal`, `Union` appear unused). This is minor but indicates interface cruft and weak hygiene.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove unused imports and run a linter.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F036  
SEVERITY: 0.57  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.54  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.update_fingerprints()` updates fingerprints only when the FSM is not terminal. The final round’s observed performance is therefore discarded, even though it may matter for auditability, postmortem diagnostics, or subsequent related runs if the manager object persists.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update fingerprints regardless of terminality, or at least record final-round observations separately.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F037  
SEVERITY: 0.56  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: `Allocation.get_assigned_models()` and `get_assigned_tasks()` use `.index()`, which raises `ValueError` for unknown IDs. There is no friendlier validation or domain-specific error message, making interface failures less diagnosable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate membership explicitly and raise a clear `KeyError`/`ValueError` with task/model context.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F038  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureType` docstring says priority ordering is by lower enum value, but actual failure dispatch is controlled by explicit if-order in `detect_failure()`. The enum numeric values are not consulted anywhere. This is misleading documentation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove the numeric-order claim or implement priority comparisons from enum values consistently.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F039  
SEVERITY: 0.54  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` emits `ROUND_COMPLETE` at the start of processing, before failure detection, metric updates, and FSM transition. The event name implies completion after processing, so the timing is semantically wrong for observers.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Emit `ROUND_COMPLETE` after processing is actually complete, and optionally add a separate `ROUND_START_PROCESSING` or `ROUND_RESULTS_RECEIVED` event if needed.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F040  
SEVERITY: 0.53  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.59  
DESCRIPTION: The module defines `default_vulnerability` in config but `CorrelatedFailureModel` never reads it. The documented “default (no correlation)” knob is dead configuration.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Thread `config.default_vulnerability` into `CorrelatedFailureModel`, or remove the config field.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F041  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.28  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManagementConfig` comments mark `blind_first` as “HARD: always start with blind round,” but the FSM ignores this flag entirely and always starts at BLIND. The parameter is misleading because it is not configurable in practice.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either remove `blind_first` or make FSM initialization depend on it.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F042  
SEVERITY: 0.51  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment.reassign()` accepts `round_idx` but never uses it. This suggests either an incomplete implementation of round-sensitive reassignment or an unnecessary parameter in the interface.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the parameter or use it in failure-history/window logic as documented.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F043  
SEVERITY: 0.50  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.estimate_gamma()` can return `inf` for equal cumulative class counts. While mathematically defensible, downstream callers may not expect infinity from a diagnostic method with no warning or explicit sentinel documentation in the return contract.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document infinity explicitly in the return semantics or return `None`/structured diagnostic metadata instead.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F044  
SEVERITY: 0.49  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.24  
DESCRIPTION: The comment in `DetectorHealthMonitor` says persistent pathologies should make the monitor “more sensitive (narrower window),” but the implementation explicitly does not reduce the window for persistent pathologies. This is internal comment contradiction.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Align comments with code or code with comments.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F045  
SEVERITY: 0.48  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.26  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.kappa()` docstring says “Conservative combination (3/4 model majority),” but `min(ks, kr, ka)` is unanimity-like across three metrics, not a 3/4-style majority. The wording is mathematically inaccurate.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the phrase with “conjunctive minimum over three metrics” or similar.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F046  
SEVERITY: 0.47  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.25  
DESCRIPTION: `DiminishingReturnsDetector.stop()` docstring says ascending abstraction guard is conjunctive, but the implementation does not use `_abstraction_dropping()` at all. The documented guard is absent from the actual predicate.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Incorporate `_abstraction_dropping()` into `stop()` as intended, or remove the claim that it is part of the implemented stop predicate.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F047  
SEVERITY: 0.46  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.53  
DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler._record_failure()` does not include the emitted detail string from detection, so failure history loses explanatory context even though `FailureRecord` supports `detail`. This weakens auditability and postmortem analysis.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Thread detail through `detect_failure()` → `get_recovery()` → `_record_failure()`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F048  
SEVERITY: 0.45  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40  
DESCRIPTION: `DetectorHealthMonitor.check_dispatch_health()` takes `round_idx` but does not use it. This suggests either missing round-local logic or unnecessary interface complexity.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Remove the parameter or use it to scope/restrict repeated diagnoses.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F049  
SEVERITY: 0.44  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.22  
DESCRIPTION: The smoke-test final print says “Phase 6 implementation complete.” but the file includes phases/areas beyond that. This is stale status messaging.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update or remove the message.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F050  
SEVERITY: 0.43  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41  
DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` imports `defaultdict` inside the function twice (`defaultdict` and aliased `_defaultdict`). This is unnecessary repeated local importing and reduces clarity.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Move the import to module scope or reuse one local import.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
